chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the people are reporting that you possess much wealth. So he said: That does not bother me.
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed one day by various people from Quraysh, and upon him was a torn shirt. They said: 'Ali has reached the morning with no wealth for him.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) heard this and ordered the one in charge of his charitable endowments to gather his dates and not send anything to anyone, and to store them. Then he said to him: Sell them to the first buyer then the next, and convert them into dirhams; then put them where you store the dates and press them in where they cannot be seen.
He said to the one who maintained the store: When I call for the dates, go up and look at the money; then strike it with your foot as if you do not intend the dirhams, until you scatter them.

Then he sent to one of those men to invite them. Then he called for the dates. When the man climbed up and was descending with the dates, he struck with his foot and the dirhams were scattered. So they said: 'What is this, O Abu al-Hasan?' He said: 'This is the wealth of the one who has no wealth.'
Then he instructed regarding that wealth and said: 'Look for the deserving ones of every household to which I used to send; look at its amount and send it to them.'

key_terms.صَدَقَتَهُ: His charitable endowment, zakah/sadaqa property held in trust
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ مُخَرَّقٌ: A torn/tattered shirt — signifying apparent poverty or asceticism
key_terms.مَا يَسُوؤُنِي: It does not harm/bother me — an expression of indifference to reputation
key_terms.مَالُ مَنْ لَا مَالَ لَهُ: The wealth of one who has no wealth — a paradoxical statement about reserved charitable funds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do when the Quraysh mocked him for being poor?
ai.summary: Abd al-A'la narrates that when he told Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that people were spreading rumors about his great wealth, the Imam responded with a story about Imam Ali (AS). When the Quraysh mocked Ali for wearing a torn shirt, Ali arranged for hidden dirhams to be dramatically scattered before them — silencing their mockery by revealing his concealed wealth. The story illustrates that public perception of poverty does not reflect hidden charitable endowments, and that a person of true piety distributes wealth to the needy rather than displaying it ostentatiously.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Murazam Bin Hakeym, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Saam who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that, the people are reporting that for you<sup>asws</sup> is a lot of wealth’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That does not bother me<sup>asws</sup>.

One day Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> passed by some people from Qureysh, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a torn shirt. So they said, ‘The morning has come to Ali<sup>asws</sup> and there is no wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> heard that and he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the one who was in charge of his<sup>asws</sup> charities that he should gather his<sup>asws</sup> dates and do not send anything from these to the people and that these should be kept aside. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Firstly sell these to the first one (buyer) and make these to be Dirhams. Then keep these where the dates were kept, and compress with it where it cannot be seen.

He<sup>asws</sup> then said to the person in charge: ‘When I<sup>asws</sup> call you with the dates, so climb and look at the wealth, so strike it with you leg as if you have no intention for the Dirhams until you scatter these’.

Then he sent for a man from them, calling them over. Then he called for the dates. So when he climbed to descend with the dates, he struck with his leg and the Dirhams were scattered. So they said, ‘What is this O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is wealth of the one who has no wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.

Then he ordered with that wealth, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Look at the deserving ones of every house which I<sup>asws</sup> used to send to them’. So they looked at his wealth, and he<sup>asws</sup> sent it (to them)’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim ibn Hakim from ‘Abd al-‘ A’la’ Mawla Ale Sam who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘People say you have a great wealth . 5

He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not affect me badly because ’Amir al-Mu’minin one day passed by different groups of Quraysh with a very old shirt on him and they said, ‘Ali has become very poor and has no assets . 5

’Amir al-Mu 5 minin heard it. He then commanded the person in charge of charity to keep his share of dates, not to send to anyone but keep them. He (the Imam) then told him to sell to the first persons who wish to buy in exchange for dirham then place the dirhams as dates are placed, then hide them with dates so they are not seen.

He then instructed the person in charge, “When I ask you for dates then climb on it, look at the asset and kick it with your foot as if you do not consider dirhams of any value and significance until they are scattered all over the place . 55

He (the Imam) then sent someone to call the people (who had called him very poor and without any assets). He (the Imam) then asked for dates. When he went to bring dates he kicked with his foot and dirhams scattered all over the place. They asked, ‘What is happening, O abu al-Hassan ? 5 He (the Imam) replied, ‘This is the assets of one who has become very poor and has no assets . 5
He (the Imam) then commanded to keep in mind the people to whom I have been sending dates. See how much were sent to each one then send that quantity to each one."
